A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JitRL research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original WebArena and Jericho evaluations, ablations, learning curves, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds controlled comparisons, parameter sweeps, and memory-scaling measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4, Appendix F, and Algorithm 1 retain the same JitRL procedure. However, Tables 15–16 introduce 'JitRL (unified)' without defining its procedure, leaving uncertainty about whether this variant changes method components or only experimental configuration.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate WebArena, WebArena-Lite, and the same three Jericho games: Library, Zork1, and Zork3. Added experiments change controls, configurations, and measurements within this coverage.

E2.justification: The new controlled WebArena-Lite comparison in Table 13 includes an untuned Llama-3.1-70B reference alongside SFT and WebRL, extending the comparator membership of the weight-update comparison. Existing baseline algorithms and original comparison tables are retained.

E3.justification: Beyond v1's existing 8B online WebRL control, Appendix J adds a shared 70B backbone with separate training and evaluation on 165 held-out tasks without test-time adaptation, plus shared-Qwen3-32B Jericho comparisons. Appendices N–Q add exploration sweeps, memory-size bins, and a GRPO protocol with 50 training steps and evaluation after each step.

E4.justification: v1 analyzes logit versus prompt updates, retrieval-neighbor count, state representations, and qualitative cases. v2 adds exploration-rate and bonus sensitivity on both benchmarks, retrieval latency and performance versus memory size, unified-pipeline comparisons, and a GRPO hyperparameter/sample-cost analysis.

E5.justification: The existing random-seed disclosure in Table 11 is unchanged, and v2 adds no repeated-seed evaluation, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 24's validation mean, minimum, and maximum summarize scores across training steps rather than independent-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original results are retained, with substantial additional results. The new offline 70B comparison reports JitRL at 40.88% versus WebRL at 46.06% (Table 13); the shared-Qwen3 comparison reports Zork1 averages of 42.1 versus GRPO's 16.2 (Table 14). Further tables add unified-pipeline, sensitivity, scalability, and tuned-GRPO results, including a best GRPO validation mean of 40.7.

T1.justification: Appendix Q.1 adds a formal definition of GRPO's group-normalized advantage in Equation 26 and distinguishes normalization across one large group from multiple smaller groups. JitRL's objectives, assumptions, theorems, and proofs in Appendices B–D remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of gradient-free continual adaptation, closed-form policy optimization, superior performance, and over 30-fold cost reduction. The added controlled results do not produce an explicit narrowing of these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning candidate generation, evaluator credit assignment, and text-based state similarity. It also qualifies applicability to offline versus continual learning, explains different exploration preferences across domains, and interprets tuned GRPO as more competitive but substantially more sample-intensive.

D1.justification: Appendix Q adds GRPO execution details including bf16, four H200 GPUs, tensor parallelism, 80-turn and 8,192-token limits, and KL coefficient 0.001. Core JitRL implementation details, prompts, default hyperparameters, and code-access information are retained. The new unified pipeline remains undefined.

R1.justification: v2 adds the ConfTuner citation by Li et al. and removes Zhang et al.'s Universal Retrieval for Multimodal Trajectory Modeling. The broader positioning against gradient-based RL and memory/prompt-based adaptation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Existing prose and section organization are largely preserved. v2 adds Limitations, Impact Statement, acknowledgements, and appendix subsections, updates cross-references, and changes correspondence and publication-header text. Most expansion consists of new scientific content rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The appendix gains substantial tabular displays for controlled comparisons, unified pipelines, exploration sweeps, memory scaling, and GRPO configurations. All five existing figures are retained. Earlier case-study and step-count tables become Tables 17–18, while Algorithm 1 and other displays are repositioned with layout and spacing adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added controls, sensitivity analyses, and specific limitations improve the paper's empirical support and clarify applicability. The gain is limited by unresolved reporting problems: the unchanged superiority claim does not reflect Table 13's 40.88% versus 46.06% offline result, and Appendix Q reports a Qwen3-32B JitRL score of 53.0 without explaining its discrepancy with Table 14's 42.1.
